teaser: Twenty-four tons of basalt, carved with stone tools, about the day the world will end.
review_notes:
Opening adapted: the sculptors are anonymous, so the lesson describes their working situation under Moctezuma II.
Diameter about 3.6 m, thickness about 98 cm, weight about 24 tons: check.
Carving date under Moctezuma II (1502-1520) and his name glyph on the stone follow current scholarship; older books date it to 1479 under Axayacatl.
Identity of the central face (Tonatiuh, or the earth deity Tlaltecuhtli) is debated; stated as such.
Function (ritual platform or vessel, possibly unfinished) is debated.
Traces of red and ochre paint reported by researchers: check.
Rediscovery on 17 December 1790; on the cathedral tower until 1885; moved to the present museum in 1964: check.
Positions of the four era glyphs (Jaguar upper right, Wind upper left, Rain lower left, Water lower right) follow standard diagrams and match the image.

lesson.text: The men who carved this had no iron, no steel, no wheel to move it and no draft animals to pull it. Their names are lost. What we know is their situation: they were stoneworkers in Tenochtitlan, the island capital of the Aztec empire, serving the ruler Moctezuma II in the early 1500s, and they shaped hard volcanic rock with harder stones, sand and water.

The block is basalt, hauled from the south of the valley on log rollers and ropes by hundreds of people. The carved disk is about 3.6 meters across (nearly 12 feet). The whole stone is about a meter thick and weighs around 24 tons, as much as four large elephants.
When it was new, it was not gray. Researchers have found traces of red and ochre paint in the grooves. Imagine it bright, under open sky.

Its popular name is the “Aztec calendar”. You could not use it to find today's date. It is closer to a diagram of time itself: how the world began, how many times it has ended, and how it will end again. Everything radiates from the face in the middle.

lesson.title: The center
lesson.text: Start where the carvers wanted you to start, and move outward one step.

spots.title: The face
spots.text: Round eyes, bared teeth, deep wrinkles. Most scholars name him Tonatiuh, the sun god. Others see the hungry earth. Both readings agree on one thing: he needs feeding.

spots.title: The tongue
spots.text: His tongue sticks out, and it is shaped like a blade. It stands for the flint knife used in sacrifice. The sun speaks in the language of offerings.

spots.title: A claw
spots.text: In the rounded lobe to the left of the face, a clawed hand clutches something. The right side has its twin. They are usually read as claws gripping human hearts.

lesson.text: The Aztecs, who called themselves the Mexica, believed the sun was not guaranteed. It had to be kept moving across the sky with the most precious thing humans could give, which was blood. A warrior people built its religion and its wars around that debt.

Around the face sit four boxes, like the blades of a windmill. Each one is a world that existed before ours and was destroyed. The carvers gave every lost world its own emblem, and you can visit them one by one.

spots.title: Jaguar Sun
spots.text: Upper right: the head of a jaguar. In the first age, the story goes, giants walked the earth, and jaguars devoured them.

spots.title: Wind Sun
spots.text: Upper left: the mask of the wind god. The second world was blown away by hurricanes.

spots.title: Rain Sun
spots.text: Lower left: the sign of the rain god. The third world ended under a rain of fire.

spots.title: Water Sun
spots.text: Lower right: the sign of water. The fourth world drowned in a flood, and its people became fish.

spots.title: The pointer
spots.text: Above the face, a sharp triangle aims straight up between the boxes, like the needle of a compass.

lesson.text: Four ages, four catastrophes. We live in the fifth, and the stone names it. The four boxes and the two claws, taken together, draw a single large sign: Ollin, which means movement. The present era is called 4 Movement, and it is expected to end in earthquakes.
The Sun Stone is not a clock but a statement: this is the fifth world, it is fragile, and it survives only as long as the sun is fed.
Aztec time ran on two calendars at once, one of 365 days for farming and one of 260 days for ritual. The two lined up again only every 52 years, a moment feared as a possible end of the world.
Move outward from the boxes and the design turns into rings, each with a job. Tracing them is the quickest way to stop the stone from looking like a maze.
From the inside out: the count of days, the rays, the frame.

lines.label: The twenty days
lines.text: A narrow band holds 20 small pictures: crocodile, wind, house, lizard and so on. These are the 20 day names of the ritual calendar, read counterclockwise.

lines.label: A ray of the sun
lines.text: Eight triangles point outward like the arms of a compass. This one, at the top, is the largest. They are the sun's rays, reaching to the edges of the world.

lines.label: A fire serpent
lines.text: The outer rim is the body of a serpent made of flame, scale after scale. A second one mirrors it on the left. They carry the sun across the sky.

lesson.text: Those two serpents begin at the top, tail to tail, and travel down either side. Follow them to the bottom of the disk and you find where they meet.
The two fire serpents meet face to face. Where are their heads?

spots.title: Jaws to jaws
spots.text: At the very bottom, two heads with open jaws confront each other. A face peers out of each mouth. At the opposite end, between the tails, a square holds a date: 13 Reed, the year the present sun was born.

lesson.text: So the stone reads from birth at the top to the confrontation at the bottom, with the endangered present in the middle. It probably lay flat, face to the sky, and may have served as a platform or a vessel for ritual. Scholars still argue about this. Notice also the uncarved rock around the disk: the block was never trimmed to a clean circle.

Then the world it described did end, though not by earthquake. Spanish soldiers and their native allies took Tenochtitlan in 1521. The stone was left lying in the main square for decades, until a bishop, uneasy about the attention it drew, had it buried face down.
It stayed underground for more than two centuries. On December 17, 1790, workers repaving the main square of Mexico City struck it with their tools, barely half a meter below the surface.

This time it was not destroyed. It was set against a tower of the cathedral, where it stood in the weather for almost a hundred years, then moved to a museum in 1885. Since 1964 it has been the centerpiece of the Museo Nacional de Antropología, and it appears on Mexican coins.

Go back to the tongue. For the people who carved it, that small blade was the most practical part of the design: the price of tomorrow's sunrise. For us it is the hardest part to look at calmly. A work of art can be magnificent and frightening at the same time, and this one does not let you choose.

quiz.question: What is the stone made of?
quiz.explanation: It is a basalt block weighing around 24 tons.

quiz.question: What does the tongue of the central face represent?
quiz.explanation: It refers to the offerings that kept the sun moving.

quiz.question: What do the four boxes around the face show?
options: Four earlier worlds that were destroyed
quiz.explanation: Jaguars, wind, fiery rain and flood ended the previous ages.

quiz.question: How is the present era expected to end?
quiz.explanation: It is named 4 Movement, the sign Ollin.

quiz.question: How was the stone found again in 1790?
options: Divers found it in a lake
Workers repaving the main square hit it
quiz.explanation: It had been buried under the square for over two centuries.

quiz.question: What runs around the outer rim?
quiz.explanation: Their tails meet at the top and their heads at the bottom.

facts.text: The Sun Stone was originally painted.
facts.explanation: Traces of red and ochre pigment have been found on it.
They had no iron and worked with stone tools, sand and water.

facts.text: The ritual calendar had 20 day names.
facts.explanation: They are shown in the ring around the center.
